issue.title: plan quotas: stamp readAt via readNow after a successful PlanQuotas read
issue.body:
### Summary

`magpie quota --json` cards that come from the **plan** path (`PlanQuotas` in `internal/provider/planquota.go`) never include `readAt`, even right after `magpie quota refresh <provider> --json`. Subscription cards (Claude / Codex) do include `readAt`. Downstream tools that gate on freshness (≤120s) therefore treat OpenCode Go and other plan providers as permanently stale.

This is not a vendor/API failure: the plan windows are populated correctly. The plan path simply never calls the existing `readNow` helper that the subscription path already uses.

### Repro

1. Configure a plan provider that uses `PlanQuotas` (example: OpenCode Go with a Go subscription key).
2. Run:
   ```sh
   magpie quota refresh opencode-go --json
   magpie quota --json
   ```
3. Observe the `opencode-go` card: `windows` has 5 hours / 7 days / Month with real `used` values, but **no `readAt` field**.
4. Compare with `claude` / `codex` cards on the same output: both have `readAt`.

(Redacted samples available on request; no keys/emails.)

### Expected

After a successful plan read (non-empty `windows`, no error), the card should carry `readAt` stamped at read time — same semantics as subscription cards.

### Actual

`ReadAt` stays `nil`. JSON export uses `omitempty`, so the field disappears entirely. `quota refresh` does not fix it.

### Root cause (from current `main`)

In `internal/provider/planquota.go`, `PlanQuotas` builds a `SubscriptionQuota`, fills `Windows` on success, then only calls `keepReading` — **never** `readNow`:

```go
q = keepReading(ctx, q, tag)
got[i] = &q
```

Subscription path already stamps via `readNow` (see `internal/provider/subscription_usage.go`):

```go
// readNow stamps a reading just made, one that doesn't say when it was
// read itself, with the time.
func readNow(q SubscriptionQuota) SubscriptionQuota {
	if q.Error == "" && q.AsOf == nil && q.ReadAt == nil && (len(q.Windows) > 0 || q.Balance != "") {
		now := time.Now()
		q.ReadAt = &now
	}
	return q
}
```

and e.g. `withUser` does `return keepReading(ctx, readNow(q), "")`.

So the fix is to align plan cards with that contract.

### Proposed fix (small)

After a successful plan window fill (and after `keepReading`, so a restored-from-disk card is not falsely stamped as "just read" unless that is intended — prefer stamping only when this fetch produced fresh windows), call the existing helper:

```go
q = keepReading(ctx, q, tag)
if q.Error == "" && len(q.Windows) > 0 && q.ReadAt == nil && q.AsOf == nil {
	q = readNow(q)
}
got[i] = &q
```

Or, if `keepReading` can restore an older `ReadAt` from disk, stamp **before** keepReading only on the success branch that just set `q.Windows`, then let keepReading preserve/merge as today. Either way: **reuse `readNow`**, do not invent a second clock.

Please also apply the same stamp on the sibling plan builders if they share the gap (`stepPlanQuotas` / `volcPlanQuotas` / `tencentPlanQuotas`), for consistency.

### Optional related ask (separate commit OK)

When a provider has **only one** key, `PlanQuotas` leaves `User` empty (`user` is set only when `len(keys) > 1`). JSON then omits `user`. Downstream UIs cannot label the card. Suggestion: for single-key plans, set `User` (or a non-secret `Alias`) from the key's display `Name` / `keyName`, **never** from the raw key material. OpenCode Go's usage API also returns no member email, so the key display name is the only stable label.

### Why it matters

Freshness gates (e.g. "reading older than 120s → do not start a costly batch") cannot trust plan cards today. Local workarounds stamp a derived fetch time and label it non-native; a one-line upstream stamp removes that split forever.

### Environment

- magpie 0.1.1650 (macOS app)
- Provider exercised: `opencode-go` (plan / OpenCode Go usage URL)
- Single OpenCode Go subscription key in this install (do not sum multiple cards)

### Checklist for a PR (if preferred over issue-only)

- [ ] `PlanQuotas` success path stamps `ReadAt` via `readNow`
- [ ] Sibling plan quota builders checked / same stamp if missing
- [ ] `magpie quota refresh <plan-provider> --json` shows `readAt`
- [ ] Subscription cards unchanged
- [ ] No key material in JSON

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/3816-plan-quota-readat` (head `3c7725cb`, on upstream `6eb510f7`) — a plan card read just now says when it was read.

**Root cause.** `internal/provider/planquota.go`'s live success never stamped `ReadAt` (`q = keepReading(ctx,q,tag); got[i]=&q`), so the card and `provider show` said nothing about when the reading happened; the same gap in `stepPlanQuota` (which builds its own windows with no keepReading) and in `tencent_usage.go`'s and `volcengine_usage.go`'s kept reads.

**Change.** `readNow` is applied where the read succeeded and `ReadAt` is still nil (so a `keepReading`-restored time is not overwritten), and unconditionally before `stepPlanQuota`'s return; `readNow`'s own error/AsOf guards keep a failed card unstamped, and the JSON shape (`readAt,omitempty`) is unchanged.

**Verified.** Red: `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider/ -run TestPlanQuotas` → `planquota_test.go:386: go read at: ReadAt:<nil>`
Green: `same command → `ok`; `TestClaudeKeptReadingKeepsItsTime` (the keepReading semantics) stays green; the package's tests pass but the pre-existing synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` (fails at base too)` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider`

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 27's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6eb510f7` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3816-plan-quota-readat — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.

issue.title: [功能建议] 为上游 API Key 设置额度保留线

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 主张

希望 Magpie 能为受支持的上游 API Key 提供可选的额度保留线：当一条有效、足够新的上游额度或余额读数达到用户设定的最低剩余值后，不再向该凭证发起新的上游尝试。

这里说的是 Magpie 自己将请求发往上游时使用的凭证，不是调用 Magpie 的 Gateway Key，也不是订阅账号的既有用量上限。

## 事实依据

- 现有 `AccountCaps` / `AccountWindowCaps` 作用于订阅账号；Gateway Key 的额度作用于 Magpie 的调用方。这两者与“某个上游 API Key 至少留多少额度”不是同一个对象或策略。
- 本机 Windows 桌面版对 MiniMax CN 做过一次真实额度验证：低于配置的保留线后，路由记录出现本地额度保护拒绝，被拦截调用的输入与输出用量均为 0。按我的现场操作手动放行后，同一会话又有成功响应；之后保护再次触发。
- 原始用量和路由日志含本机的会话信息，因此没有附到 issue。程序只保留最近一次人工动作，不能从持久状态独立还原点击放行的时间；手动放行是我的现场操作记录。

## 理据

Magpie 决定了每次上游尝试实际使用哪个凭证，也能在请求发送前检查对应读数。若读数已触及用户设定的保留线，路由就可以阻止后续发送，避免继续消耗用户想保留的额度。

这不要求预测单次请求会消耗多少，也不要求把尚未发生的消耗预留出来；保留线只是一个以已接受的上游读数为依据的准入条件。

## 支撑与相关议题

- [#1606](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/1606) 提出给会话预留账号/Key，并把新会话分流到其他凭证；其中也讨论了额度底线。本议题关注的行为不同：触线后停止该凭证的所有新物理尝试，不为已固定的会话保留例外。
- [#1772](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/1772) 讨论额度耗尽后仍反复向上游请求的问题。本议题关注的是在触及上游限额前，按用户设置的保留线停止新尝试。
- [#2745](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/2745) 讨论 Key 额度与钱包余额的区分，和额度指标的来源、范围有关；它没有提出凭证级保留线。
- [#3816](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3816) 讨论计划额度读数的时间戳，和读数新鲜度有关；它没有提出按保留线阻止请求。

这些议题提供相关背景，但都不是本需求本身。

## 适用范围与边界

- 只有在上游读数有效、足够新且能明确映射到受保护凭证时，才依据该读数判断是否触线。
- 上游读数可能滞后，因此该策略不能保证真实账户余额永远不低于保留线。
- 已经准入并正在执行的请求不因此被强行取消；不确定是否已送达上游的请求也不应仅为额度保护而重放。
- 不应把额度保护与用户手动启停、上游错误退避混成同一种状态。
- 不应静默改变既有订阅账号上限的默认语义。

## 期望行为

1. 用户可以按受支持的上游额度窗口或余额设置最低剩余值，并明确其单位。
2. 达到保留线后，该凭证不再收到新的物理上游尝试，包括同一逻辑请求后续可能发生的尝试。
3. 若存在其他符合现有路由条件的凭证，请求可以继续交给它；若全部触线，Magpie 返回可识别的本地拒绝，不把它记成上游故障。
4. 手动关闭的凭证仍保持关闭；未知、无效或过期读数不能被当作额度充足。
5. 若提供人工放行或重新启用，应是明确操作，且不能改变用户手动开关或掩盖未知读数。

## 请维护者判断

这份需求限定的是可观察行为，没有要求一定新增独立配置文件、GUI 区块或策略存储。额度策略应放在 Provider Key、复用现有额度上限，还是接入其他已有抽象，以及状态怎样纳入备份与同步，请维护者结合 Magpie 现有功能决定。

issue.title: Remote magpie provider: a subset of its quota cards never re-read (used + readAt frozen for 10+ min)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Summary

When the Mac app uses a **remote magpie as a provider** (a `remote-magpie` preset pointed at another machine's gateway), some of that remote gateway's quota cards stop refreshing. After the initial read they freeze — both `used` values and `readAt` — for tens of minutes, while other cards on the same remote provider keep refreshing normally.

The remote gateway itself is healthy: hitting its `GET /v1/magpie/quotas` directly with the same gateway key returns fresh values for **every** card, every single time.

So the freeze happens in the **local app's polling/aggregation layer**, not in the remote gateway and not at the vendor.

### Environment

- magpie **0.1.4303** (macOS app, arm64, macOS 26.4.1) — also reproduced on 0.1.4287 and 0.1.4283
- Local: Mac app, Settings → Allowances: **Allowance reads = Automatic**, menu bar refresh = **1 min**
- Remote: magpie **0.1.4292** in Docker on another machine, reached over a tailnet hostname, configured as a `remote-magpie` provider (`gz`)
- The remote gateway key has `quotas: true`, so the local app is allowed to read its quotas

### Cards observed (all from the same remote provider `gz`)

| Card | Kind | Auto-refresh |
|---|---|---|
| `gz/kimi` | plan | ✅ refreshes every ~1-2 min |
| `gz/~keys` | plan (key balance) | ✅ refreshes constantly |
| **`gz/volcengine`** | plan | ❌ **frozen** |
| **`gz/ollama-cloud`** | plan | ❌ **frozen** |
| **`gz/ollama-cloud`** | balance | ❌ **frozen** |
| **`gz/clinepass`** | balance | ❌ **frozen** |

Also frozen, on the other remote provider: `vps/claude` (subscription), stuck at a `readAt` from two days earlier.

### Repro

1. Configure a remote magpie (another machine) as a provider, with a gateway key that has quotas enabled.
2. Make sure at least one of its providers is a **`plan`** card that needs an **access key** for its usage read (e.g. Volcengine Ark Agent Plan via `access.key` / `access.secret`) — and also have a plain **`balance`** card on the same remote.
3. Leave the app idle and sample the local gateway:

```sh
while true; do
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/magpie/quotas \
    | jq -c '.data[] | select(.provider|startswith("gz/")) | {provider,kind,readAt,u:(.windows[0].used)}'
  sleep 20
done
```

4. Observe: `kimi` and `~keys` advance; `volcengine`, `ollama-cloud` (plan and balance), and `clinepass` stay pinned to the same `readAt` and same `used` for 10+ minutes.
5. At the same instant, sample the **remote** gateway directly with the same key:

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REMOTE_KEY" http://<remote-host>:3425/v1/magpie/quotas \
  | jq -c '.data[] | {provider,kind,readAt,u:(.windows[0].used)}'
```

6. The remote returns fresh `readAt` and fresh `used` for all cards — including `volcengine`.

### Evidence (one session, 15:39 → 15:53 local time)

Remote, read directly at 15:52:25:

```
volcengine  readAt=15:52:25  used=[5 hours 19.288, Weekly 5.511, Month 46.507]
```

Local, immediately after, still showing the earlier read:

```
gz/volcengine  readAt=15:39:21  used=[5 hours 16.474, Weekly 4.707, Month 46.226]
```

Then over the next 60 seconds, sampling every 15 s, `gz/volcengine` did not move at all:

```
15:52:51 readAt=15:52:25 used5h=19.288
15:53:06 readAt=15:52:25 used5h=19.288
15:53:21 readAt=15:52:25 used5h=19.288
15:53:37 readAt=15:52:25 used5h=19.288
```

A 90-second no-traffic window on a different run showed three cards advancing while four stayed pinned — confirming this is selective, not a full stall:

```
changed:    gz/ollama-cloud(plan), gz/kimi, gz/~keys, vps/~keys
unchanged:  gz/volcengine, gz/ollama-cloud(balance), gz/clinepass(balance), vps/claude(subscription)
```

### Narrowing down: the 30 s throttle path

`magpie quota refresh gz/volcengine --json` immediately after a read returns this, and does not update the card:

```
read 14s ago: not asked again before 30s have passed, shown as it was read
magpie: no subscription, plan or key balance of gz/volcengine · magpie quota lists them
```

That `read %s ago: not asked again before %s have passed, shown as it was read` string is the throttle, and the second line says magpie does not consider `gz/volcengine` to *have* a subscription, plan or key balance at all — even though the card, with real windows and real `used` values, is sitting right there in the same list.

So the two symptoms look like one cause:

- The card is present and populated, but the local app's view of "does this provider have an allowance to poll?" comes back negative for it — hence never polled again.
- The throttle then refuses to re-read it and reports the stale value as if fresh.

### Expected

For a remote provider whose gateway key has `quotas: true`, **every** quota card the remote gateway serves should be polled on the same cadence as the others, and `readAt` / `used` should advance together. If a card genuinely cannot be read, it should say so (`error`) rather than silently presenting an old value as current.

### Actual

A subset of the remote provider's cards is never re-read. The values silently age while the card gives no indication it's stale. Switching **Allowance reads** between `Automatic` and `When I ask`, and upgrading 0.1.4283 → 0.1.4287 → 0.1.4303, did not change the behaviour.

### Workarounds that do help, partly

- Quitting and relaunching the app re-reads everything once; the frozen cards then go stale again.
- `magpie quota refresh <provider>` works only when the 30 s throttle has elapsed, and only for cards it agrees are pollable — which excludes exactly the frozen ones. In practice the frozen cards only refresh when an app restart happens to force it.
- Reading the remote gateway directly (`GET /v1/magpie/quotas` with the key) always returns correct, fresh data — so the data path itself is fine.

### Notes

This looks adjacent to but distinct from #3816 (plan cards missing `readAt`). Here `readAt` **is** present on the frozen cards — it just stops advancing. Happy to pull more traces, redacted, if useful; no keys or identifiers included in this report.
